title: Local Orchestrator: UX & API Sketchbook
content:
Purpose:
Quick, messy sketchbook for the local orchestrator UX surface + a compact API sketch for a thin agent that runs next to customer apps. Trying to reconcile two constraints: (1) developer-facing ergonomics (fast feedback, readable errors) and (2) runtime affordances (prefetch, KV cache hints, tenant affinity).

High-level goals (intended):
- Low-friction onboarding for devs: single binary/sidecar with minimal config to wire up to hosted/Dedicated/Private.
- Predictable local behavior: deterministic fallback ordering, visible metrics for decisions.
- Small, testable API shape for request routing, prewarm/prefetch hints, and session-snapshot interactions.

Notes / heuristics:
- Keep agent API primarily HTTP+JSON; protobuf only internally or for long-term perf.
- Control plane signals (rollouts, model variant preference) should surface via the same agent API (prefetch/annotations) to avoid separate websocket config complexity for devs.
- Prefer explicit small payloads for prefetch hints (no embedding blobs in agent requests).

Rough API surface (single file):
POST /v1/invoke
- body: { "session_id": "s-12345", "instr": { ... }, "hints": [ ... ], "mode": "stream|sync" }
- returns: 202 accepted + location /v1/invoke/{call_id} for streaming

Small example payload (illustrative):
{
  "session_id": "local-abc-42",
  "instr": {
    "prompt": "Summarize latest onboarding notes for user.",
    "max_tokens": 256,
    "temperature": 0.0
  },
  "hints": [
    { "type": "prefetch", "key": "user:123:kb:latest", "ttl_s": 60 },
    { "type": "kv-affinity", "key": "session-ctx-v1", "expected_size": 1024 }
  ],
  "mode": "stream"
}

Agent introspection endpoints (debug-only):
GET /v1/health -> { status, active_model, last_prefetch_ts }
GET /v1/session/{id}/manifest -> returns compact manifest of cached keys, prefetch hints, pinned model variant
POST /v1/snapshot (for offload) -> body: { session_id, snapshot_meta } returns { snapshot_id, checksum }

Config sketch (local agent config, porteable -> YAML-like):
agent:
  listen: 127.0.0.1:2777\  # default developer only port\  telemetry: local\  fallback_policy:
    - prefer_local_variant
    - route_to_hosted_if_unavailable
  prefetch:
    enabled: true\    budget_tokens_per_minute: 5000\    default_ttl_s: 30
  kv_cache:
    max_entries: 10k\    eviction: lru
  dev_mode: true

Decision rationale: keep the config small and opt-in. If dev_mode=false, agent obeys conservative budget and disables verbose traces.

Interaction sketch (ASCII sequence diagram):
App -> Agent: POST /v1/invoke (session+prompt+hints)\Agent -> AgentScheduler: decide route (local/dedicated/hosted)\AgentScheduler -> KVCache: check prefix hits\AgentScheduler -> Prefetcher: enqueue prefetch tasks (if hints present)\Agent -> RemoteEndpoint: forward request (if needed)\RemoteEndpoint -> Agent: stream tokens / structured output\Agent -> App: stream tokens to client

UX: developer-visible surfaces to implement first (MVP):
1) Local CLI: redwood-local status, tail logs, request replay mode\2) Web UI: simple flow showing last 20 invocations, cached keys, model variant chosen, latency breakdown\3) Instrumentation: include a compact call_id and cost-estimate header returned on every response

Open questions (quick):
- How much of the prefetch DSL do we expose to customers vs keep internal? I think a small typed set (prefetch/kv-affinity/prompt-hint) is fine.
- Should snapshots be chunked vs atomic? chunked snapshots cheaper but rehydration complexity.
- What is the minimal set of telemetry we can collect in dev_mode=false to preserve PII-safety?

Edge cases / gotchas observed during trials:
- Large prefetch budgets can unfairly load local GPU in Dedicated setups; default small budgets and explicit opt-in for heavy prefetch.
- Session_id collision in dev environments when SIDs are auto-generated by frameworks (need short, randomized suffix).
- Simulated network flaps exposed a race between snapshot writes and cache eviction (add write-ahead manifest).

Mini decision log (chronological):
2024-11-10: Prototype: plain http agent + in-memory KV. Fast to iterate but loses across restarts.
2024-11-18: Add snapshot endpoint + manifest to keep cross-process restore simple.
2024-12-01: Introduced hints array (prefetch/kv-affinity). Only accept small payloads to avoid hidden embedding transfers.

Next steps (practical):
- Implement /v1/session/{id}/manifest and add a CLI command to force-evict a key. (owner: Priya)\- Wire minimal web UI that reads /v1/health + last 20 calls (owner: Darren)\- Draft a short RFC for snapshot chunking tradeoffs, include rehydration cost estimates (owner: Maya)

TODO (personal):
- write unit tests for Prefetcher quotas\- test worst-case when prefetch queue grows under heavy concurrency\- sketch a simple fallback-language for canary rules (route modelX->modelY on latency>300ms)

Random implementation notes (brain dump):
- Use a compact manifest format: list of (key, size, last_used_ts, pinned_variant) instead of full metadata to speed up restore.
- When in dev_mode, return a special header X-Redwood-Dev-Hint with the route decision and rationale: helps debugging.
- Consider a lightweight signed snapshot token so private deployments can accept snapshots from local dev securely.

End of sketchbook entry. This is intentionally rough — meant for rapid follow-ups and a starting point for a short RFC.
